title: Who Allah is
hook: Not a cop waiting for you to slip. Someone closer to you than you think.

screens.text: You've learned how to pray. Today is about **who you're praying to**. Some people grow up picturing God as distant, or as a cop waiting for them to slip. That isn't the God the Qur'an describes.

**Allah is near.** When people asked the Prophet ﷺ about Allah, the answer came in the Qur'an:

> "Indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me." [Q 2:186, Saheeh Intl.]
bubbles: Another verse says Allah is closer to you than your own jugular vein [Q 50:16].
You never need a middleman, a special place or perfect Arabic to reach Him.

screens.prompt: What does Allah say about Himself in [Q 2:186]?
screens.feedback: He's near, and He answers whoever calls Him.

screens.text: **Allah is merciful, more than you can picture.** The Prophet ﷺ said Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent only one to earth. All the kindness between people and animals comes from that one part [Muslim 2752].
bubbles: He also taught that Allah says: if you come toward Him walking, He comes to you running [Bukhari 7405].

screens.before: Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent

options.feedback: Yes. All the kindness on earth comes from one part. He kept the other ninety-nine.
Not quite. Only one part came to earth. Imagine the ninety-nine He kept.
Not quite. Just one part came to earth, and He kept the other ninety-nine.

screens.prompt: Allah has many names in the Qur'an. Match each name to its meaning.

pairs.right: The Most Gracious, whose mercy covers everything
The Most Merciful, especially kind to those who turn to Him

screens.text: You'll say two of these names in every prayer: *ar-Rahman, ar-Rahim* is the third verse of al-Fatiha [Q 1:3]. Others come in pairs in the Qur'an: **the Forgiving, the Loving** [Q 85:14], and **near and responsive** [Q 11:61].
bubbles: Allah is also just, and He sees everything. But the Qur'an tells even people who've done wrong never to lose hope in His mercy [Q 39:53].

screens.prompt: Dre feels he's messed up too much for Allah to want to hear from him. What fits what you learned today?

options.text: Allah is near and answers whoever calls Him, so Dre can turn to Him right now
options.feedback: Yes. Allah answers whoever calls [Q 2:186] and tells us never to lose hope in His mercy [Q 39:53].

options.text: He should fix his life first, then start talking to Allah
options.feedback: Not quite. You don't clean up first and then come. You come, and Allah helps you clean up.

options.text: He needs someone more religious to pray for him
options.feedback: Not quite. Others can pray for you too, but you never need a middleman. Allah is near [Q 50:16].

screens.text: **What you believe, in one breath.** Muslims believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and His decree, the good and the hard [Bukhari 50]. These six are called the articles of **iman** (faith).
bubbles: You'll explore each one in Phase 2. For now, the first one is enough: knowing who Allah is.

screens.title: Du'a: talking to Allah
screens.intro: **Du'a** (a personal prayer) is talking to Allah in your own words, in any language, any time: in bed, on the bus, after your salah.

steps.text: Ask Him for anything, big or small

screens.done_text: The five prayers have set words. Du'a is yours.

screens.prompt: Write your first du'a: a few lines to Allah in your own words. Thank Him for something, and ask Him for one thing you need right now. Then say it, quietly.

chips: If Allah is merciful, why is there suffering?
Is Allah the same God Christians worship?
Does Allah hear du'a in English?
Why does the Qur'an say 'We' for Allah?

screens.text: Make one du'a today, in your own words.
steps: Pick a moment: right after a prayer, before you get up, is a good one
Thank Him for one thing, and ask Him for one thing
screens.optional_extra: Pick one of today's names and notice it in your day. When something kind happens, think: ar-Rahim.

screens.text: Allah is near, merciful, loving and forgiving. You can talk to Him any time, in your own words.
You don't have to be perfect to come close to Allah. You just have to keep coming.

options.text: A personal prayer to Allah, in your own words and any language
options.feedback: Right. Du'a can be made any time, about anything.

options.text: Only the Arabic words of the five prayers
options.feedback: Not quite. The five prayers have set words, but du'a is your own, in any language.

check.prompt: According to the Qur'an, how close is Allah to you?

options.feedback: Right [Q 50:16]. And He answers whoever calls Him [Q 2:186].

options.text: Far away, reachable only through religious leaders
options.feedback: Not quite. Allah is near and answers you directly [Q 2:186].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Allah is near and answers whoever calls Him [Q 2:186]; closer than the jugular vein [Q 50:16]; "near and responsive" [Q 11:61]; "the Forgiving, the Loving" [Q 85:14]; ar-Rahman ar-Rahim [Q 1:3].
- Mercy in a hundred parts, one sent to earth [Muslim 2752]. Allah comes running to the one who walks to Him [Bukhari 7405]. Never despair of His mercy [Q 39:53].
- The six articles of faith from the Hadith of Jibril [Bukhari 50]. Detail comes in Days 31–43.
- About one in four US converts hold a "distant, unforgiving, cop-like" image of God, linked to lower practice [Yaqeen 2025]. This lesson exists to counter it.
- Allah has no gender; "He" is a grammatical convention, and the Qur'an's "We" is the plural of majesty [Revealed Path ch. 8].

**Likely questions**
- *"Why is there suffering?"* Short, honest: life is a test; hardship isn't a sign Allah doesn't care; Day 43 (destiny) goes deeper. Don't lecture someone in pain; ask how they are.
- *"Same God as Christians?"* Muslims believe in the God of Abraham, Moses and Jesus; Arab Christians call Him Allah. Muslims differ from Christian belief on the Trinity and Jesus's nature (Day 27). Respectful tone.
- *"Du'a in English?"* Yes, any language, any time.
- *"Why 'We'?"* Plural of majesty, not more than one God.
- *"Does Allah love me after what I did?"* Muslim 121 (Day 1), Q 39:53. Warm, no listing sins.

**Escalate:** anyone describing despair, self-harm or hopelessness (safety rule 6 first).

**Don't:** use Hell to motivate; claim to know anyone's fate; overload with all 99 names; say Allah is "like" a person.
